meta.description: Tests gene lists, ranked vectors, and fold-change vectors against KEGG pathways and modules with clusterProfiler enrichKEGG/enrichMKEGG (ORA), gseKEGG (GSEA), and SPIA/graphite (signed-topology perturbation) in R. Covers why a KEGG result is a timestamped join against a live REST API, why enrichKEGG keyType is kegg/ncbi-geneid not OrgDb ENSEMBL/SYMBOL, why organism is a KEGG code with prokaryotic locus tags, and why SPIA works only on signaling maps.
meta.environment: R 4.4.3 / Bioconductor 3.20 (F:\OpenScience\audit-envs\crispr-screen-analyst); clusterProfiler 4.14.6, org.Hs.eg.db 3.20.0, gson 0.2.1, SPIA 2.58.0, graphite 1.52.0, pathview 1.46.0, KEGGREST 1.46.0 -- same environment as the pre-fix audit, no packages changed. Data: byte-identical copies of the pre-fix audit's own SYNTHETIC_de_results.csv / SYNTHETIC_eco_de_results.csv (verified via diff before use), used here as regression fixtures against the fixed Skill.

This auditor did not audit or fix the pre-fix version and has no stake in this Skill passing. 5 of 7 inputs are direct regressions of pre-fix inputs (re-run against the fixed code, same data, same prompts); 2 are new: Input 5 (determinism double-run of the new set.seed() fix) and Input 3 doubles as the redundancy-pass check (Common Organism Codes table, moved from usage-guide.md into SKILL.md, sourced and verified using SKILL.md alone). scientific_integrity.detail: References unchanged from pre-fix (8 real, correctly attributed papers). No DOI/PMID, p-value, sample size, or effect size invented anywhere in the fixed Skill or in any of my 7 runs; every number in this report came from a run recorded under run/.

practice_boundaries.detail: Unchanged from pre-fix: pure functional-genomics/bioinformatics methodology, nothing diagnoses, prescribes for, or triages an individual.

methodological_ground.detail: The three methodological claims verified pre-fix still hold (universe-omission bias reproduced identically: 170 vs 136 pathways, 135/135 shared pathways more significant without background, Input 7; ID-join failure mode reproduced identically, pre-fix Input 6 code path unchanged; gson pinning idempotency reproduced identically, pre-fix Input 5 code path unchanged). Pre-fix's minor wording imprecision (SPIA on metabolic maps) is now corrected in SKILL.md. NEW finding this round (Input 4/4b), not a veto trigger but recorded as a P1: with the graphite route now actually running for the first time (it crashed 100% of the time pre-fix), it computes a perturbation direction (Activated/Inhibited) that DISAGREES with the direct spia() route on 30/99 (30%) of pathways scored by both, including one of the audit's own two ground-truth planted pathways (hsa04110/Cell cycle: direct spia() correctly calls Activated matching the planted UP direction, tA=+67.4; graphite calls the same pathway Inhibited, tA=-66.7). This is a real, reproducible divergence between two topology sources (not a bootstrap-noise artifact -- tA is deterministic given the graph and fold-changes, confirmed identical across reruns in Input 5), not a fabrication or an invalid statistical model -- topology databases are known in the literature to disagree on edge sign/direction for the same biological pathway -- but SKILL.md presents the graphite route as simply 'the modern route' with zero caveat that it can call perturbation direction oppositely from the primary spia() path. Scored as a documentation-completeness gap (P1), not a methodological fallacy, so does not fail this dimension.

Did you forget to run prepareSPIA?', 0 usable rows). Independently reproduced in run/in4_spia_and_graphite_fix.out and, twice with identical results, in run/in5_determinism_check.out. key_strengths: The pre-fix P0 is genuinely, verifiably fixed: the graphite+runSPIA pattern, which crashed 100% of the time pre-fix (in both SKILL.md's own text and the shipped example), now runs unmodified (except an audit-turnaround-only nB reduction) and returns 191 real, non-degenerate scored pathways -- confirmed independently in three separate runs (Input 4, Input 5, and gate 8's byte-verbatim example execution).

Both pre-fix P1s are fixed and independently re-verified under repeated invocation, not just as text changes: set.seed(123) now precedes both spia() and runSPIA(), and a dedicated determinism double-run (Input 5) confirms bit-identical output across reruns for both routes; the missing refuse/warn instruction for a missing background gene set is now an explicit Agent Workflow step, confirmed present in the fixed SKILL.md and functionally exercised in Input 7.

The redundancy pass (usage-guide.md -> SKILL.md) lost nothing an agent needs: verified both by a direct diff against the pre-fix skill_copy (every deleted usage-guide.md passage traced to its new SKILL.md home, confirmed present) and by an executed redundancy-pass check (Input 3) that sourced the moved Common Organism Codes table from the fixed SKILL.md alone and got the correct prokaryote result.

6 of 7 unchanged-or-fixed code paths reproduced their pre-fix numeric results to the reported precision (ORA 136 pathways/hsa04110 p.adjust=2.13e-35, GSEA NES +-3.6, prokaryote eco00010 p.adjust=3.65e-84, no-universe bias 170 vs 136), giving strong confidence the fix and redundancy pass introduced no regression.

recommendations.title: graphite route disagrees with direct spia() on perturbation direction for 30% of pathways, undocumented
recommendations.problem: Now that the P0 crash is fixed and the graphite route actually runs, it computes an opposite-sign perturbation (Activated vs Inhibited) from direct spia() for 30 of 99 pathways scored by both, including one of the Skill's own two ground-truth planted pathways (hsa04110/Cell cycle: graphite says Inhibited, direct spia() and the planted direction both say Activated). SKILL.md presents the graphite route as simply an interchangeable 'modern route' with no caveat that it can reach a different scientific conclusion.
recommendations.root_cause: This divergence was undiscoverable before this fix round because the graphite route never completed a single successful run pre-fix (Research Veto M4 FAIL); the fixer's own verification (fixes/bio-pathway-kegg-pathways.md) checked that runSPIA returned real rows but did not cross-check its direction calls against the direct spia() route.
recommendations.fix: Add a caveat to the SPIA section (and the Common Errors / Per-Method Failure Modes tables) stating that graphite's harmonized topology can disagree with SPIA's native KEGG-bundled topology on perturbation direction for a meaningful fraction of pathways, and recommend treating the two routes as complementary evidence rather than interchangeable, or explicitly stating which one to prefer as the default and why.

recommendations.title: Shipped SPIA example defaults to nB=2000, no smaller value suggested for quick iteration
recommendations.problem: examples/kegg_spia_topology.R's default n_boot=2000 makes a full run of the direct spia() + graphite sections take substantially longer than the other examples in this Skill; an agent following the shipped example verbatim on a first exploratory pass has no documented lighter-weight option.
recommendations.root_cause: n_boot is hardcoded to SPIA's own package default without a documented fast-iteration alternative.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line comment noting that nB can be lowered (e.g. to 200-500) for interactive exploration and should be raised back to 2000+ only for the final reported result, mirroring the practice this and the fixer's own verification already use.
